claims.quote: The key to avoiding this difficulty is to introduce a novel logical operation P ∗ Q,called separating conjunction (or sometimes independent or spatial conjunction),that asserts that P and Q hold for disjoint portions of the addressable storage.
claims.states: Separating conjunction P ∗ Q asserts that P and Q hold for disjoint portions of memory.

claims.quote: p0 ∗ p1 asserts that the heap can be split into two disjoint parts in which p0 and p1 hold respectively
claims.states: Formally, p0 ∗ p1 holds of a heap if the heap splits into two disjoint parts, one satisfying p0 and the other p1.

claims.quote: emp asserts that the heap is empty
claims.states: The assertion emp holds exactly of the empty heap.

claims.quote: asserts that the heap contains one cell,at address e with contents e′
claims.states: The points-to assertion e ↦ e′ holds of a heap with exactly one cell, at address e, holding e′.

claims.quote: if the current heap is extended with a disjoint part in which p0 holds,then p1 will hold in the extended heap
claims.states: The separating implication (magic wand) p0 −∗ p1 holds if adding any disjoint heap satisfying p0 yields a heap satisfying p1.

claims.quote: neither contraction, p ⇒ p ∗ p,nor weakening, p ∗ q ⇒ p,are sound. Thus separation logic is a substructural logic.
claims.states: In Reynolds's (classical) separation logic, p ∗ q does not entail p and p does not entail p ∗ p, so the logic is substructural.

claims.quote: Unfortunately,however,the rule of constancy is not sound for separation logic.
claims.states: Hoare logic's rule of constancy (conjoining an unmodified assertion with ∧) is unsound once heaps can alias, which motivates the frame rule.

claims.quote: Thus,the frame rule is the key to “local reasoning” about the heap
claims.states: The frame rule {p} c {q} / {p ∗ r} c {q ∗ r} is what makes local reasoning about the heap possible.

claims.quote: which O’Hearn calls the footprint of c
claims.states: The variables and heap parts a command actually uses are called its footprint, a term Reynolds attributes to O'Hearn.

claims.quote: If we start execution with a state that has additional heap cells, beyond those described by P , then the values of the additional cells will remain unaltered.
claims.states: Heap cells beyond those a precondition describes are left unchanged by the command, which is what the frame rule records.

claims.quote: This enables the initial specification {P }C{Q} to concentrate on only the cells in the program’s footprint.
claims.states: Because of the frame rule, a specification need only mention the cells in the program's footprint.

claims.quote: Ishtiaq and O’Hearn devised a classical version of the logic that is more expressive than the intuitionistic version. In particular, it can express storage deallocation.
claims.states: The classical version of separation logic is more expressive than the intuitionistic one and can express deallocation.

claims.quote: separating conjunction asks for a partitioning that divides the heap into parts, heaplets, satisfying its two conjuncts
claims.states: A separating conjunction holds when the heap can be partitioned into heaplets that satisfy each conjunct.

claims.quote: emp is the unit of ∗, so that P = emp ∗ P = P ∗ emp.
claims.states: emp, the assertion that the heaplet is empty, is the unit of separating conjunction.

claims.quote: −∗ is an implication quantifying over separate heaps
claims.states: The magic wand is an implication that quantifies over heaps separate from the current one.

claims.quote: Assume a partial commutative monoid (H, ◦, e), where ◦ : H × H ⇀ H and e ∈ H.
claims.states: The semantics of separation logic assumes states form a partial commutative monoid with a partial combining operation and a unit.

claims.quote: In the RAM model H is the set of finite partial functions from positive integers (addressible locations) to integers, h ◦ h′ is the union of functions with disjoint domain, and undefined when h and h′ overlap.
claims.states: In the RAM model, heaps are finite partial maps and combining two heaps is defined only when their domains are disjoint.

claims.quote: To understand how a program works, it should be possible for reasoning and specification to be confined to the cells that the program actually accesses. The value of any other cell will automatically remain unchanged.
claims.states: The principle of local reasoning confines reasoning and specification to the cells a program accesses; O'Hearn proposed it in the 2001 CSL paper.

claims.quote: allows a proof to be localized to the resources that a program component accesses (its footprint)
claims.states: The frame rule lets a proof be localized to a component's footprint.

claims.quote: giving rise to the Infer static analyzer, a tool that is in deployment at Facebook where it catches thousands of bugs per month before code reaches production in products used by over a billion people daily
claims.states: Separation logic underlies Facebook's Infer, which catches thousands of bugs per month before production.

claims.quote: One of these, Verifiable C, is the foundation of Appel’s Verified Software Toolchain
claims.states: Verifiable C, a higher-order concurrent separation logic, underlies Appel's Verified Software Toolchain (VST).

claims.quote: Iris has been used to provide a foundation of the type system of the Rust programming language
claims.states: Iris has been used as a foundation for Rust's type system.

claims.quote: A separation algebra is a cancellative, partial commutative monoid (Σ, •, u) .
claims.states: A separation algebra is a cancellative partial commutative monoid.

claims.quote: A partial commutative monoid is given by a partial binary operation where the unity, commutativity and associativity laws hold
claims.states: A partial commutative monoid has a partial binary operation satisfying unit, commutativity and associativity laws.

claims.quote: The cancellative property says that for each σ ∈ Σ, the partial function σ • (·) : Σ ⇀ Σ is injective.
claims.states: Cancellativity means combining with a fixed state is injective.

claims.quote: An example of a permission algebra is the interval (0, 1] of rational numbers, with ◦ being addition but undefined when permissions add up to more than 1.
claims.states: Fractional permissions form a permission algebra: rationals in (0,1] under addition, undefined when the sum exceeds 1.

claims.quote: Every PCM is an RA, but not vice versa
claims.states: Resource algebras generalize partial commutative monoids.

claims.quote: Instead of partiality, RAs use validity to rule out invalid combinations of ownership.
claims.states: An RA's composition is total; a validity predicate marks which combinations are allowed.

claims.quote: Instead of having a single unit ε that is an identity to every element (i.e., that enjoys ε · a = a for any a), RAs have a partial function |−| that assigns to an element a its (duplicable) core |a|
claims.states: Instead of a single unit, an RA has a partial core function giving each element its duplicable part.

claims.quote: In the special case that an RA does have a unit ε, we call it a unital RA (uRA).
claims.states: A unital RA is an RA that has a unit element ε.

claims.quote: It is worth noting that the global RA must be unital, which means it should have a unit element ε (Figure 3).
claims.states: Iris requires the global resource algebra to be unital.

claims.quote: Note that one can always turn an RA into a unital RA by extending it with a unit element, preserving all frame-preserving updates.
claims.states: Any RA can be made unital by adding a unit, without losing frame-preserving updates.

claims.quote: Iris always maintains the invariant that the state obtained by composing the contributions of all threads is a valid RA element. We call state changes that maintain this invariant frame-preserving updates.
claims.states: A frame-preserving update is a ghost-state change that keeps the composition of all threads' resources valid.

claims.quote: the task of the exclusive RA E X (X ) is to make sure that one party exclusively owns a value x ∈ X
claims.states: The exclusive RA ensures only one party owns the value; any composition of two elements is invalid.

claims.quote: the task of the agreement RA A G 0 (X ) is to make sure multiple parties can agree upon which value x ∈ X has been picked
claims.states: The agreement RA lets several parties share and agree on one value.

claims.quote: Persistent propositions can be freely duplicated ( PERSISTENT - DUP ); the usual restriction of resources being usable only once does not apply to them.
claims.states: Persistent propositions can be duplicated freely, unlike ordinary resources.

claims.quote: Iris is an affine separation logic, which means that it enjoys the weakening rule P ∗ Q ⇒ P. Intuitively, this rule lets one throw away resources
claims.states: Iris is affine: P ∗ Q entails P, so resources may be thrown away.

claims.quote: in traditional classical separation logic it is guaranteed that allocated memory has been freed since one cannot throw away points-to predicates
claims.states: Linear (classical) separation logic can prove absence of memory leaks because points-to facts cannot be discarded.

claims.quote: Iris is a framework for higher-order concurrent separation logic, which has been implemented in the Coq proof assistant and deployed very effectively in a wide variety of verification projects.
claims.states: Iris is implemented in Coq and used in many verification projects.

claims.quote: A resource algebra is a commutative semigroup M together with a subset V ⊆ M of elements called valid, and a partial function | · | : M → M, called the core.
claims.states: A resource algebra is a commutative semigroup with a set of valid elements and a partial core function.

claims.quote: A resource algebra is unital if M is a commutative monoid with unit ε and the following properties hold.
claims.states: A unital RA has a unit ε, which must be valid and be its own core.

claims.quote: A canonical example of a unital resource algebra is the one of heaps.
claims.states: Heaps form a unital RA: composition is disjoint union, overlap gives the invalid element, and the empty heap is the unit.

claims.quote: The non-trivial compositions are only m · m = m and otherwise (when m and n are distinct) m · n = ⊥.
claims.states: In the agreement-style RA, an element composed with itself is itself, and distinct elements compose to the invalid element.

claims.quote: The operation is defined such that x·y = ⊥ for all x and y.
claims.states: In the exclusive RA every composition is invalid.

claims.quote: However the valid elements are only those q less than or equal to 1
claims.states: The fractions RA has positive rationals under addition, with only q ≤ 1 valid.

claims.quote: It states that any element compatible with a is compatible with some element in B.
claims.states: A frame-preserving update a ⇝ B holds when every frame compatible with a is compatible with some b in B.

claims.quote: P ∧ Q ` P ∗ Q if P is persistent.
claims.states: If P is persistent, P ∧ Q entails P ∗ Q (the ` is ⊢ garbled by extraction).

claims.quote: if one of the propositions is persistent, then there is no difference between conjunction and separating conjunction
claims.states: Since P ∗ Q always entails P ∧ Q, ∧ and ∗ coincide when one side is persistent.

claims.quote: Persistent propositions are important because they are duplicable
claims.states: Persistent propositions are duplicable (rule persistently-dup: □P ⊣⊢ □P ∗ □P).

claims.quote: The roots of the approach are in Boyland’s [3] demonstration of the utility of fractional permissions in specifying non-interference between concurrent threads.
claims.states: Permission accounting in separation logic builds on Boyland's 2003 fractional permissions (Boyland 2003 was not read).

claims.quote: a permission is z, where 0 < z ≤ 1; z = 1 allows dispose, write and read; any other value is read access only.
claims.states: A fractional permission is in (0,1]; 1 allows write and dispose, smaller fractions allow only reading.

claims.quote: Any fractional permission less than 1 prescribes passivity
claims.states: A fraction below 1 guarantees the command cannot change the cell.

claims.quote: Infer, as we will discuss, uses one analysis based on the theory of Separation Logic
claims.states: One of Infer's analyses is based on separation logic.

claims.quote: the fix rate rocketed to over 70%
claims.states: Run at code review (diff time), Infer's reported issues were fixed over 70% of the time, versus near zero in batch mode.

claims.quote: the separating conjunct , to allow denotating that assertions hold over disjoint subsets of the heap
claims.states: Kiran's blog explains the separating conjunct as asserting that assertions hold over disjoint parts of the heap.

claims.quote: All it asserts is that there exists some partitioning of the entire heap, such that one can make spatial assertions P and Q both true.
claims.states: P ** Q holds when some partition of the heap makes P and Q true on the parts.
